draft.title: Enzymes as catalysts
card: Enzymes are proteins that speed up chemical reactions in cells. They are catalysts, so they are not used up and can work again and again.
Every reaction needs a push to get started, called the activation energy. An enzyme lowers the activation energy, so the reaction happens faster at body temperature.
The substrate is the molecule an enzyme acts on. It binds to the active site, a small region of the enzyme with a particular shape and chemistry.
In the induced fit model, the active site changes shape slightly as the substrate binds, so it grips the substrate more closely. The enzyme then releases the products.
draft.remember: Enzymes speed up reactions by lowering activation energy, and each binds its own substrate at its active site.

a.q: How does an enzyme make a reaction in a cell go faster?
opts: It lowers the activation energy of the reaction
It raises the energy of the substrate molecules
It is used up as it supplies energy to the reaction
It changes the products into different molecules
a.why: A catalyst works by lowering the activation energy, so more collisions lead to a reaction. The enzyme is not used up, so the option saying it is consumed is wrong.
a.clue: Think about the push needed to start a reaction.

b.q: Tariq studies an enzyme that breaks down a sugar. When the sugar binds, the active site shifts slightly and closes around it. Which statement best fits this observation?
opts: It fits the induced fit model, as the active site adjusts
It shows the enzyme is used up as the sugar binds
It shows the active site is a rigid shape that never changes
It shows the enzyme raises the activation energy
b.why: In the induced fit model, the active site changes shape as the substrate binds. A rigid, unchanging active site would contradict what Tariq saw. Enzymes lower activation energy and are not used up.
b.clue: Look at what the active site does when the sugar binds.

a.best: It lowers the activation energy of the reaction

b.best: It fits the induced fit model, as the active site adjusts

2.alt: Energy against the progress of a reaction, without an enzyme (dashed) and with an enzyme (solid). An arrow points down from the higher peak to the lower one.
